messages:
maria: Quick heads-up — saw p95 spike on hosted API at ~18:10 UTC, correlates with last-night coalescer window change. p95 jumped ~120ms -> ~320ms for a subset of tenants. p99 mostly unchanged. Any theories?
aj: Can you paste the metric slice and any logs? which coalescer config did we flip?
maria: Rolling metric slice: queue_depth.avg 0.8 -> 3.6, p95_latency 120ms -> 320ms, kernel_swap_rate +0.6/s on affected hosts. Coalescer.delay_ms changed from 5 -> 25 at 01:12 UTC during staged rollout.

maria: log snippet from one affected host: ```
[2024-11-12T18:10:32Z] req_id=ab12 host=gpu-17 "batch_start" batch_size=1 coalescer_wait_ms=22 kernel_choice=v2 kernel_swap_ms=11 kv_cache_hit=false
[2024-11-12T18:10:32Z] req_id=ab12 "enqueue_time_ms" 4 queue_depth=3
[2024-11-12T18:10:32Z] req_id=ab12 "complete" latency_ms=312
```
aj: Hmm kernel_swap_ms=11 is suspicious. Increasing coalescer window can increase batching but also increases chances of kernel mismatch and swap. devon: also looks like coalescer allowed more small batches to coalesce into mixed-dtype batches that trigger kernel swap. we added the epoch-based kernel swap optimization but it doesn't prevent on-the-fly swaps for mixed batches.

devon: quick thought — the small tenants with bursty 1-2 token requests end up waiting, then when they flush they create mixed batches with bigger tenant requests. coalescer=25ms reduced throughput uniformity and increased tail.
samir: I also see per-shard kv cache churn on those hosts. eviction_rate +80% during spike window. when kv miss occurs we recompute embeddings that increase infer time and can flip kernel path (quant->fp path).

aj: can we confirm if those tenants are on the same shard? affinity map shows 3 tenants hitting shard-9 across noisy tenant set. 
maria: yes — shard-9 hotness score jumped from 0.12 -> 0.68. coalescer change coincided with noisy neighbor traffic pattern (long-context requests from tenant X).

maria: quick repro command (from dev cluster): ```bash
for i in {1..200}; do 
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"input":"short"}' https://hosted.redwood/api/v1/generate &
done
```
Run with a mix of short and 512-token requests to emulate mixed batches.
aj: Suggested immediate mitigation: rollback coalescer.delay_ms to 8ms for hosted fleet (not full rollback to 5ms) and turn on kernel-lock-for-mixed-batches feature flag to avoid on-the-fly kernel swaps. Also add limit on per-shard concurrent heavy requests (soft cap).

maria: I'm +1 to rollback to 8ms and enable kernel-lock flag on staged hosts. timeline: rollback now on 10% canaries, measure p95.
luca (oncall): doing 10% rollback now.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: Started rollout: coalescer.delay_ms=8ms -> canary(10%) by maria at 2024-11-12T18:45:10Z. Rollout id=rl-20241112-001.
maria: initial canary shows queue_depth.avg -> 1.1 and p95 trending toward 140ms on canaries (within 10m). keeping an eye.
samir: opened follow-up ticket INF-5723: "coalescer heuristics: avoid kernel swap regressions for mixed-batch hotspots". Includes profiling artifacts and per-tenant shard map.

devon: action items: 1) rollback to 8ms (in progress) 2) instrument per-tenant kernel_swap_count metric 3) add KV eviction + request-size correlation panel on runtime dashboard 4) longer-term: coalescer aware of tenant affinity and kernel compatibility.
aj: I'll add a short perf test to the CI that simulates mixed-size churn and checks kernel_swap_rate < 0.1/s.
luca (oncall): ack. keep posting if p95 changes. :thumbsup:
maria: thanks all — will update thread after full rollout.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: Rollout rl-20241112-001 completed at 2024-11-12T19:12:03Z. Canaries -> 100%.
